answer: Scaled dot‑product attention first takes a query vector and computes its dot product with each key vector, producing a similarity score for every key[Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention]. Each score is divided by the square root of the key dimension (√d_k) to stabilize gradients, and the resulting values are passed through a softmax function, which converts them into normalized weights that sum to one[Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention]. These softmax weights are then used to form a weighted sum of the corresponding value vectors, yielding the final attention output[Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 4, §3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention].
